title: ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-17.1.56).
evidence: Saved search uc_17_1_56_ise_radius_change_of_authorization_coa_f, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

compliance.controlObjective: Incident-response closure evidence for change-of-authorization workflows.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Misconfigure CoA shared secret on a lab NAD. Apply ANC quarantine to an endpoint on that NAD. ISE emits 5419 (CoA failed) and the NAD emits %RADIUS-3-COA_NACK. UC-17.1.56 fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Fix the shared secret. Quarantine succeeds via 5417/5418. Alert clears.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Authentication* category — CoA codes `5417` (CoA initiated), `5418` (CoA succeeded), `5419` (CoA failed), `5420` (CoA timeout), `5421` (CoA NAS not responding). Fields: `coa_action` (port-bounce|port-shutdown|reauth|disconnect), `NAS-IP-Address`, `endpoint_mac`, `error_code`. NAD-side: `index=network sourcetype=cisco:ios` `%RADIUS-3-COA_NACK`. CIM mapping: `Change.action`.
app: `Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)) + Cisco network TA.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (5417, 5419, 5420, 5421))
  OR (index=network sourcetype="cisco:ios" "%RADIUS-3-COA")
| eval action = case(MessageCode=="5417", "initiated", MessageCode=="5419", "failed", MessageCode=="5420", "timeout", MessageCode=="5421", "nas_no_response", like(_raw, "%COA_NACK%"), "nas_nack")
| stats count by NAS-IP-Address, action, coa_action
| where action != "initiated" AND count > 5
description: Detects RADIUS CoA failures, timeouts, and NAS no-response events at scale. CoA is how ISE pushes runtime authorization changes (quarantine, reauth, port-bounce) to NADs — failures mean the enforcement action didn't reach the device.
value: When SOAR pushes a quarantine to ISE and ISE pushes a CoA to the NAD that fails, the endpoint *remains uncontained*. CoA failure detection is the closure validation for incident-response automation.
implementation: Confirm *Authentication* category at INFO. Schedule every 5 min, search window `-15m@m to @m`, throttle suppression on `NAS-IP-Address` for 30 min.
visualization: (1) Single value: CoA failures last 1h. (2) Top-N NADs by failure count. (3) Failure-class breakdown.

references.title: RFC 5176 — Dynamic Authorization Extensions to RADIUS

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• NAD configured with `aaa server radius dynamic-author` (and matching shared secret).
• `nad_inventory.csv` with `nas_ip`, `coa_supported`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Validate event flow.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 5 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — CoA Health":
• Single value: failures last 1h.
• Top-N NADs.
• Failure-class.

Alerting: PagerDuty medium on sustained CoA failure for one NAD.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **Shared-secret mismatch** — Realign on NAD and ISE.
• **NAS no response** — UDP/3799 (or 1700) blocked.
• **CoA initiated but NAD doesn't enforce** — NAD has `aaa authorization network ... default group ...` not configured to honour CoA.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)) + Cisco network TA.). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, cisco:ios into nac, network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`NAS-IP-Address, action, coa_action`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: When ISE tells a switch 'kick this person off the network' via a special message, we make sure the switch actually heard the message and acted on it.
